Constantia - Life Insurance Cancelled!

By: Julian Sun | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We highlight the plight of over 5000 consumers who've had their life insurance policies cancelled by Constantia Insurance

Unique Selling Point:
To provide a platform to showcase the outrageous behaviour of Constantia Insurance who in 2020 cancelled 2 of their Life Insurance products: Prime Living Cover Grow & Living Legacy leaving over 5400 people without life insurance

Summary:
Between 2010 and 2018, Constantia Insurance Company Ltd sold two short term insurance products to over 5000 customers in the open market. These products were marketed through various media outlets and physical brochures. Beyond this marketing, potential customers were sold the policies telephonically.

In 2017, the Short Term Insurance Act 53 of 1998 (STIA) and the Long Term Insurance Act 52 of 1998 (LTIA) were repealed and replaced with the Insurance Act 18 of 2017 (IA), which took effect on 1 July 2018. The IA compelled every insurer to elect whether to operate a life insurance business or a non-life insurance business. To this effect, the IA contained transition provisions which allowed insurers to convert their licenses obtained in terms of STIA or LTIA to whichever mode of insurance they elected to continue selling under the IA. The transition provisions included a lengthy process whereby an insurer could transfer its non-life insurance business to another company if it elected to continue with life insurance business (and vice versa).

Constantia elected to conduct a non-life insurance business and it considered transferring the policies to a company in the same holding company. The companies decided that the transfer would not be feasible as it would require an increase in premiums for the take-over to be affordable to it. Consequently, Constantia decided to cancel the policies. It sent SMS notifications to approximately 5348 policyholders cancelling the policies and indicating that an expert would provide an explanation and alternatives in due course.

Further information:
On 27 July 2020, the PA directed CICL to extend the existing policies until 31 August 2020 and thereafter offer a replacement policy, which provided cover for personal accidental death and extended funeral benefits. Accidental death cover and funeral cover are relatively cheap and in light of the age and health condition of the policyholders, the replacement policy provided substantially reduced the benefits due in comparison to the Living Legacy and CoverGrow policies. Particularly, at this stage of their lives, the policyholders are more likely to pass away from an illness or natural causes rather than an accident, in which case they would not be covered by the replacement policy. The policholders currently have no life cover. In instances where policholders have already passed away, CICL have rejected claims on the basis that the policies are no longer in existence. Their familiaes have been unjustly deprived of the financial security that their loved ones intended to leave behind.

Press Release:


Life Cover Stripped
Life insurance policies are meant to protect families and loved ones; buy peace of mind – ensuring financial security, helping to leave an inheritance or pay off debts and expenses. So how could the life insurance of thousands of policy holders, many elderly and with pre-existing conditions suddenly be cancelled last year – leaving clients high and dry? Carte Blanche investigates a short-term insurer that promised “Cover for Life, without ever increasing your premiums” but in 2020 suddenly cancelled the policies of thousands of their clients by sms. Now scores of clients are taking the fight all the way to demand accountability for devastating losses they’ve incurred.
Producer: Julian Sun | Presenter: Claire Mawisa

Script:


OPENING LINK: A life insurance policy gives you security with the knowledge that your family will be financially taken care of when you pass away. But what do you do when that peace of mind is taken away?

V/O: That’s the nightmare scenario that has befallen 5427 people, many elderly or with pre-existing conditions. They had bought either the Living Legacy or the Prime Living Covergrow Policies from a 3rd party broker Prime Meridian Direct. The policies were underwritten by Constantia Insurance Company Limited. From 2010 to 2018, these policies were marketed via tele-sales as products that provide cover for life with fixed monthly premiums.




V/O: It was an attractive offer for Able & Martinique Kaye because she suffers from an autoimmune disease called Myasthenia gravis

Martinique explains her condition

and how she felt peace of mind in the knowledge that when she passes away, she’d be leaving R5 million to her children

Abel says it was so attractive that he has spent of R250 000 in premiums since he bought it for his family
V/O: Gillian Niemiec’s wife Amanda has suffered with cancer for the past 18 years.

Gillian explains Amanda’s cancer had made her uninsurable so when they saw an advert for Living Legacy while shopping in a mall, they jumped at the opportunity

Gillian tells us that Amanda’s cancer treatment is very expensive and when she eventually passes away, it will be left to her to pay the outstanding medical bills – that’s why the insurance policy was so valuable to them

V/O: For years, policy holders faithfully paid their monthly premiums safe in the knowledge that their families would be protected in the event of an unexpected death through accident or illness.

Then in 2017, parts of the Short Term Insurance and Long Term Insurance Act were repealed and replaced by the Insurance Act.

This had serious implications for all policy holders, as attorney Arno Botha explains.

Arno Botha explains that changes to the law meant that insurance companies couldn’t offer both life and non-life products. They had to choose which business they wanted to be in.

Constantia Insurance decided to be a non-life company only, meaning that by law, they could no longer offer the Living Legacy or Covergrow policies.

V/O: The effect was that, as of July 2020, Constantia would no longer be able to provide these policies, as they did not fall within the categories of policies that a non-life insurer can provide. Policy holders were notified by SMS

Gillian & Martinique react to the cancellation of their policies

V/O: 31 year old Lupus sufferer Samantha Brett was also surprised when her policy was cancelled

Best comments about how all attempts to contact Constantia to find out what was going on led to frustration and disappointment

















V/O: We asked Prime Meridian Direct for comment. They wrote back to say that “Constantia’s decision to cancel the policies was taken unilaterally and without our prior knowledge or any forewarning. PMD first became aware of the decision when affected policy holders began contacting our offices to query and complain against the termination notices received from Constantia”
They went on to further state that “Throughout this time, PMD’s brand and reputation has suffered immeasurable harm.


V/O: In June 2020, an application was launched at the High Court by dozens of policy holders. Constantia submitted that, “the amendments required to the policies to bring them in line with the Insurance Act were so significant that it would not be tenable or in the interest of the policyholders for Constantia to do so.
As a result, Constantia elected to cancel the policies and had the right to do so in terms of the policies themselves.
However Judge Bashier Vally ruled in favour of the policy holders and declared that the cancellation of the policies by Constantia to be unlawful

He ordered them reinstated and for Constantia to submit the policies to the Prudential Authority (the body that regulates insurance in South Africa) as part of the licence conversion process


Case studies react to the replacement policy[DM4]

V/O: With Constantia having offered a replacement, the Prudential Authority considered the matter to be “orderly resolved”, leaving all policyholders without life cover.



V/O: In a last bid for recourse, 104 former policy holders have now taken the case to the Financial Services Board Tribunal and asked for the matter to be reconsidered

Sonam Mansingh from Richard Spoor Incorporated will be part of the legal team that will represent them at the hearing set for October

Sonam explains their submission to the FSB

LINK: We reached out to Constantia for an on camera interview but unfortunately they declined citing that “as the matter is currently pending before the tribunal and they felt it would be inappropriate to do so”
















V/O: They did provide us with a written statement saying: “Constantia has continued to take guidance from the Prudential Authority regarding the policies that were exclusively sold by PMD, an independent third-party broker. Throughout this, we have been clear that our principal focus was (and is) about operating strictly within the regulatory guidelines. We will continue to do so"

The PA also declined our request for an interview stating: The Prudential Authority maintains the view that it would not be appropriate for it to make any pronouncement on this matter, as it is currently before the FSB.




Comment from Gillian



Case studies tell of their inability to secure insurance from anywhere else.[DM5]

Case studies on what they would like to say to Constantia


Arno & Sonam outline possible outcomes

Best comment from case studies about what they would like to achieve

PROMO 1: Why was the life insurance of thousands of policy holders, many elderly and with pre-existing conditions suddenly cancelled last year - leaving clients high and dry? We investigate how it happened.

PROMO 2: We investigate a short-term insurer that promised “Cover for Life, without ever increasing your premiums” but then last year suddenly cancelled the policies of thousands of their clients by sms.

PROMO 3: What are scores of policyholders with one short-term insurer going to do to fight against the cancellation of their life insurance policies that they had staked their financial security on?
